# Phase 1 — Rename `assignee_id` to `owner_id`

Blocks on: none.

## What this makes work

Every place that stored, read, or asserted on `assignee_id` now uses `owner_id`, with no behavior
change. Check: `node --test` passes with the renamed field, and `grep -ri assignee` over the repo
returns nothing outside this plan's own files and the spec/glossary prose that explains the rename.

## Context

- `docs/specs/csat-rating.md:14,25` — requirement 6 and its acceptance criterion.
- `src/tickets.js:14,28,42` — the field is set in `createTicket`, written in `assignTicket`, read in
  `reopenTicket`.
- `docs/glossary.md:14` — the glossary entry "Assignee" already says the assignee is the agent who
  owns the ticket; the spec cites this as the reason for the rename.
- Answered validation question 1 (see `plan.md`): rename the field and direct references to it only;
  leave `assignTicket`/"assign" wording alone.

## Files to modify

- `src/tickets.js` — `assignee_id` → `owner_id` at the three sites above.
- `test/tickets.test.js:20,24` — the assertion on `t.assignee_id`; the test name on line 24 ("the
  assignee hears of it") can stay, since it's describing the verb, not the field (per question 1).
- `test/export-tickets.test.js:21` — the destructured `r.assignee_id` in the row-shape assertion.
- `docs/glossary.md:14` — reword the "Assignee" entry to "Owner", keeping its definition sentence.

## Steps

1. In `src/tickets.js`, rename all three `assignee_id` occurrences to `owner_id`.
   Evidence: `grep -n assignee_id src/tickets.js` returns nothing.
2. Update `test/tickets.test.js` and `test/export-tickets.test.js` to read `owner_id` instead of
   `assignee_id`.
   Evidence: `node --test` passes (paste the summary line).
3. Rename the glossary entry "Assignee" to "Owner" in `docs/glossary.md`, keeping the same
   definition text ("The agent who owns the ticket. A ticket in the unassigned queue has no
   owner.").
   Evidence: diff shown to the user.
4. Confirm no other file still mentions `assignee_id` or the field under its old name.
   Evidence: `grep -rin assignee .` from the repo root shows only this plan's own prose (if any) and
   the spec file, which documents the historical name on purpose.

## Exit criteria

- `node --test` passes.
- `grep -rin assignee_id .` from the repo root returns nothing.
- `docs/glossary.md` calls the concept "Owner".

## Risks

- The real production store is Postgres (per `src/store.js:2`'s comment); this repo has no
  migration tooling or migration files, so the actual `assignee_id` → `owner_id` column rename on
  that table is out of scope for this plan and needs its own migration, coordinated separately
  before this code ships against production. Flagging this now so it isn't missed at deploy time.

# Phase 2 — Customer rates a resolved ticket

Blocks on: Phase 1 (needs `owner_id`).

## What this makes work

A customer can submit a 1–5 rating for a resolved ticket of their own organisation, once; a score
of 1 or 2 queues an email to the ticket's owner. Check: the acceptance-criteria tests listed below
pass under `node --test`.

## Context

- `docs/specs/csat-rating.md:9-14,18-23` — requirements 1-4 and their acceptance criteria.
- `src/portal.js:10-14` — `getMyTicket` already returns `null` for a nonexistent ticket or one
  outside the customer's org; reuse it so "wrong org" and "doesn't exist" stay indistinguishable,
  satisfying the spec's acceptance criterion on that point for free.
- `src/portal.js:21-28` — `reply` is the existing precedent for throwing a descriptive `Error` on an
  invalid status transition (`'this ticket is closed; please open a new one'`); follow the same
  style for the new refusals.
- `src/tickets.js:33,40` — `resolveTicket`/`reopenTicket` throw ``cannot <verb> a ${t.status}
  ticket`` for a bad status; match that phrasing for consistency.
- `src/notify.js:6-9` — `notifyAgent(store, agentId, event)`; throws if `agentId` is falsy, so guard
  the call the same way `reopenTicket` guards it at `src/tickets.js:42`.
- Answered validation question 2 (see `plan.md`): only a `resolved` ticket can be rated; closed is
  refused the same way open/pending is, via a thrown error, not the null path.
- Answered validation question 3 (see `plan.md`): new fields are `rating_score` (integer 1-5 or
  `null`) and `rated_at` (ISO string or `null`).

## Files to modify

- `src/portal.js` — add `rateTicket(store, customer, id, score, { now } = {})`.
- `src/tickets.js` — no change needed; `STATUS.RESOLVED` is already exported.
- `test/tickets.test.js` — add the rating tests (or a new `test/rating.test.js`; either is fine,
  this plan uses a new file to keep `tickets.test.js` focused on ticket lifecycle).

## Steps

1. Add `rateTicket` to `src/portal.js`:
   - Look up the ticket via `getMyTicket(store, customer, id)`; return `null` if that's `null`
     (covers "doesn't exist" and "wrong org" identically).
   - If `score` is not an integer from 1 to 5 (`!Number.isInteger(score) || score < 1 || score >
     5`), throw `Error('score must be a whole number from 1 to 5')`.
   - If `t.status !== STATUS.RESOLVED`, throw ``Error(`cannot rate a ${t.status} ticket`)``.
   - If `t.rating_score != null`, throw `Error('this ticket has already been rated')`.
   - Otherwise `store.updateTicket(id, { rating_score: score, rated_at: now.toISOString() })`.
   - If `score <= 2` and `t.owner_id`, call `notifyAgent(store, t.owner_id, { type:
     'ticket_rated_low', ticketId: id, score })`.
   - Return the updated ticket (re-read via `getMyTicket` for the `messages` shape, matching
     `reply`'s return convention).
   Evidence: code reads as above; shown in the diff.
2. Write the acceptance-criteria tests, one per bullet in the spec:
   - 4 on a resolved ticket of the customer's own org stores `rating_score: 4` and a `rated_at`.
   - A non-integer/out-of-range score (`0`, `6`, `3.5`) throws.
   - Rating an `open` ticket throws `cannot rate a open ticket`; a `pending` one throws likewise.
   - Rating a `closed` ticket throws too (question 2's answer).
   - A second rating attempt on an already-rated ticket throws, and `rating_score`/`rated_at` are
     unchanged from the first call.
   - Rating via `globex` on a ticket opened by `acme` returns `null`, same as a made-up ticket id.
   - A score of 2 adds one entry to `drain()`; a score of 3 adds none.
   Evidence: `node --test` output, pasted, showing all new tests passing.
3. Run the full suite once more to confirm Phase 1's rename didn't regress and nothing else broke.
   Evidence: `node --test` summary line pasted (count of passing tests).

## Exit criteria

- All seven acceptance-criteria bullets for requirements 1-4 have a passing test.
- `node --test` passes with no regressions in the existing suite.

## Risks

- `resolveTicket(store, id, agentId)` doesn't actually require `owner_id` to be set — a ticket can
  be resolved while still unassigned. The notify-on-low-score step guards on `t.owner_id` being
  truthy (same pattern as `reopenTicket`), so an unassigned-but-resolved ticket's rating is stored
  but no email is queued. Worth a one-line note in the PR description so it isn't read as a bug.

# Phase 3 — Nightly weekly rating summary

Blocks on: Phase 2 (needs `rating_score`/`rated_at` to exist).

## What this makes work

A nightly job writes, per agent, how many ratings their tickets received in the trailing seven days
and the average score. Check: the acceptance-criteria test below passes under `node --test`, and
running the job writes a readable file under `exports/`.

## Context

- `docs/specs/csat-rating.md:13,24` — requirement 5 and its acceptance criterion (ratings 5, 4, 1 →
  3 ratings, average 3.33; an eight-day-old rating doesn't count).
- `src/jobs/export-tickets.js` — the direct precedent: a nightly job that scans
  `store.listTickets()` and writes one JSON file under `EXPORT_DIR` (`exports/`), with a test that
  reads the file back from a temp dir (`test/export-tickets.test.js:12-13`).
- `src/jobs/close-resolved.js:8-16`, `src/jobs/purge-closed.js:10-19` — the pattern for a "nightly,
  windowed by `now`" job: `now.getTime() - new Date(t.<field>).getTime() < WINDOW` to skip rows
  outside the window, with `now` injectable for tests.
- Answered validation question 4 (see `plan.md`): write `exports/agent-ratings.json`, one row per
  agent with ≥1 rating in the trailing 7 days, shape `{ owner_id, ratings, average_score }`,
  average rounded to 2 decimals; agents with zero ratings in the window get no row.

## Files to create

- `src/jobs/weekly-summary.js` — the new job.
- `test/weekly-summary.test.js` — its test.

## Files to modify

- `README.md` — add the new job to the "Three jobs run every night" list (it becomes four).

## Steps

1. Write `src/jobs/weekly-summary.js`:
   - `const WINDOW_DAYS = 7; const DAY = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;`
   - `weeklySummary(store, { dir = EXPORT_DIR, now = new Date() } = {})`.
   - Scan `store.listTickets()`, keep rows where `rating_score != null` and `now.getTime() - new
     Date(t.rated_at).getTime() < WINDOW_DAYS * DAY`.
   - Group the kept rows by `owner_id`; for each group compute `ratings = group.length` and
     `average_score = Math.round((sum / group.length) * 100) / 100`.
   - Skip any group with a `null`/missing `owner_id` (a rated ticket should always have one by the
     time it's resolved and rated, but guard anyway rather than emit a row with no agent).
   - Write the rows to `<dir>/agent-ratings.json` via `fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })` +
     `fs.writeFileSync`, mirroring `export-tickets.js:11-13`.
   - Return `{ file, agents: rows.length }`, matching `exportTickets`'s `{ file, rows }` return
     convention.
   Evidence: code shown in the diff; shape matches `export-tickets.js`'s conventions.
2. Write the acceptance-criteria test in `test/weekly-summary.test.js`: one agent with ratings 5, 4,
   1 inside the window and one rating 8 days old; assert the written file has exactly one row for
   that agent, `ratings: 3`, `average_score: 3.33`, and the 8-day-old rating isn't counted.
   Evidence: `node --test` output, pasted, showing the test passing.
3. Add a second test: an agent with zero ratings in the window gets no row (not a zero-valued row).
   Evidence: same `node --test` output.
4. Update `README.md`'s job list to mention `src/jobs/weekly-summary.js` and what it writes.
   Evidence: diff shown to the user.

## Exit criteria

- The acceptance-criteria bullet for requirement 5 has a passing test, including the "eight days
  old is not counted" edge.
- `node --test` passes end to end (all three phases' tests together).
- `README.md` lists four nightly jobs.

## Risks

- None beyond Phase 1's migration note, which already covers the new `rating_score`/`rated_at`
  columns needed for this job to have anything to read in production.

===== docs/plans/261006-0932-csat-rating/plan.md =====
# CSAT rating — implementation plan

Spec: `docs/specs/csat-rating.md` (approved, Mai Do, 2026-01-12).

## Goal

A customer can rate a resolved ticket 1–5 from the portal, once; a low score (1–2) emails the owning
agent; a nightly job writes each agent's trailing-7-day rating count and average. Along the way,
`assignee_id` becomes `owner_id` everywhere.

## Validation questions (answered with my recommendation; nobody has confirmed these — flagged "assumed" in each phase)

1. **Does the rename reach beyond the literal field?** Recommend: rename the stored field and every
   direct reference to it (code, tests, the glossary term "Assignee" → "Owner"). Leave the function
   name `assignTicket` and the verb "assign" alone — the spec names the field, not the verb, and
   renaming the verb too would ripple without being asked for.
2. **Can a closed ticket still be rated?** Recommend: no — only `resolved`. The spec's requirement 1
   says "a resolved ticket"; closed is terminal per the glossary ("if the customer comes back, they
   start a new ticket"). Refused the same way open/pending is refused (a thrown error), not the
   null/not-found path.
3. **What are the new fields called, and does the low-score email block the save if it fails?**
   Recommend: `rating_score` (integer 1–5 or `null`) and `rated_at` (ISO string or `null`) on the
   ticket row, matching `resolved_at`/`closed_at`. The email is queued in-process via the existing
   `notifyAgent` (no network call, can't fail independently), so no transactional concern.
4. **Where does the nightly summary get written, and in what shape?** Recommend: follow
   `export-tickets.js`'s pattern — `exports/agent-ratings.json`, one row per agent with at least one
   rating in the trailing 7 days: `{ owner_id, ratings, average_score }`, average rounded to 2
   decimals. Agents with zero ratings in the window get no row.

## Phases

| # | Phase | Status | ACT/COUNCIL | Blocks on |
|---|-------|--------|-------------|-----------|
| 1 | [Rename assignee_id to owner_id](phase-01-rename-owner-id.md) | not started | ACT | none |
| 2 | [Customer rates a resolved ticket](phase-02-rate-ticket.md) | not started | ACT | Phase 1 |
| 3 | [Nightly weekly rating summary](phase-03-weekly-summary.md) | not started | ACT | Phase 2 |

No phase touches auth, payments, migrations, or tenancy code directly (the portal's existing
org-scoping in `getMyTicket` is reused, not changed), so none of this needs an independent
pre-push review under the hot-path list. The rename and the new `rating_score`/`rated_at` fields
are a real schema change for the production Postgres table behind `store.js`; this repo only has
the in-memory store, so that migration is out of scope here and called out as a risk in Phase 1.

## Key dependencies

- Phase 2 reads/writes `owner_id`, so it needs Phase 1 done first.
- Phase 3 reads `rating_score`/`rated_at`, so it needs Phase 2 done first.
- All three phases run against `node --test` (the only guardrail this repo has: `npm test`).

## Next step

`bk-build` on Phase 1 — it has no blockers.
